brand.title: LoOG Record Book
brand.dek: Nine seasons on the books. Every win, every collapse, every trophy — and the head-to-head ledger that settles the group chat.
brand.description: Nine seasons of League of Ordinary Gentlemen fantasy football - champions, all-time standings, head-to-head records and single-week extremes.
notes: Reconciled against ESPN. All 96 season rows in the original spreadsheet match the box scores exactly on wins, losses, points for and points against, as do every champion and runner-up. Three fields did not, and use the ESPN figures here: playoff appearances (the sheet undercounted six — six teams make the bracket every year, so the total is 54) and division titles (Karen 3→2, Kaila 2→1). Every last-place finish is as the league recorded it.

Last place means two different things by era, matching how the league actually awarded it. From 2017 to 2021 it went to the worst regular-season record. From 2022 — when the league grew to twelve teams and added a consolation bracket — it goes to whoever finished last in the final standings. 2024 had none recorded and is filled in under the 2022-onward rule.
Seasons finishing exactly .500 are counted as their own category rather than as losses, which moves Karen from four losing seasons to three.
